The topmost circle is x; the second layer has two empty circles; the third layer has three circles, of which the rightmost one is 27; the fourth layer has four circles, of which the leftmost one is 7 and the rightmost one is 15; the bottom layer has five circles, visible from left to right as 2, 5, empty, empty, 6. Problem rule explanation: The number in each circle is equal to the sum of the numbers in the two adjacent circles below it. Reasoning: Let the bottom layer from left to right be 2, 5, b3, b4, 6. Also a3 = b3 + b4 = b3 + 9, so b3 = 3. Thus the bottom layer is 2, 5, 3, 9, 6. The fourth layer is 2+5=7, 5+3=8, 3+9=12, 9+6=15. The third layer is 7+8=15, 8+12=20, 12+15=27. method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a 5-level triangular number pyramid with top circle x. From the image, note the visible values: bottom row has 2, 5, blank, blank, 6; the row above has 7 at the far left and 15 at the far right; the row of three has 27 at the far right. Use the text rule that each circle equals the sum of the two circles directly below it, and work locally upward/right-to-left by subtraction: since the far-right row-above-bottom circle is 15 and the bottom-right circle is 6, the adjacent missing bottom value is 9. Since the far-right circle in the row of three is 27 and its lower-right supporting circle is 15, its lower-left supporting circle is 12. That 12 is the sum of the missing bottom-middle value and 9, so the missing bottom-middle value is 3. Then fill the remaining pyramid upward by addition: 2+5=7, 5+3=8, 3+9=12, 9+6=15; next row 7+8=15, 8+12=20, 12+15=27; next row 15+20=35 and 20+27=47; top x=35+47=82.
